name: Question 2
problem: The air temperature $F$ in degrees Fahrenheit can be modeled by the function $F(C)=\frac{9}{5}C+32,$ where $C$ is the air temperature in degrees Celsius. Find the instantaneous rate of change of the air temperature in degrees Fahrenheit with respect to the air temperature in degrees Celsius.

Question 2
?

The air temperature F in degrees Fahrenheit can be modeled by the function F(C)=95C+32, where C is the air temperature in degrees Celsius. Find the instantaneous rate of change of the air temperature in degrees Fahrenheit with respect to the air temperature in degrees Celsius.

a
59 degrees of Fahrenheit per degree of Celsius
b
95 degrees of Fahrenheit per degree of Celsius
c
1695 degrees of Fahrenheit per degree of Celsius
d
2939 degrees of Fahrenheit per degree of Celsius
e
5169 degrees of Fahrenheit per degree of Celsius
Submit
